{{Quote|You said the rakghouls were caused by a ''plague''&mdash;do you mean a disease?''"<br />"''Magic is the vector, but a rakghoul bite or scratch carries a disease, like a virus. It doesn't matter. There is no cure.|[[Cade Skywalker]] and [[Celeste Morne]]|<ref name="LegacyVector" />}}
The '''rakghoul plague''', alternatively referred to as the '''rakghoul disease''' or '''rakghoul virus''', was a [[Disease/Legends|disease]] [[Sith alchemy/Legends|engineered]] by the ancient [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Karness Muur]]. Muur, seeking a means to escape [[Death/Legends|death]] and achieve [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] conquest, forged a [[Sith talisman/Legends|Sith amulet]] that came to be known as the [[Muur Talisman]], an item into which Muur poured his mind, will, and [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]]. The Muur Talisman's power could almost instantaneously turn any nearby [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] being into a mindless [[rakghoul]], a [[Sithspawn/Legends|Sith-spawned]] [[mutant]] subservient to Muur's will. But the talisman's power was not perfect, and it could not transform [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]] or beings belonging to certain [[Alien/Legends|non]]-[[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Species/Legends|species]] into rakghouls, and thus Muur designed the rakghoul plague to compensate for this weakness. The [[virus]]-like plague, carried by every rakghoul in existence at the time, could be spread to another being by a [[Tooth/Legends|bite]] or a scratch from a rakghoul's [[Claw/Legends|claw]]. The victim would then suffer through an incubation period lasting approximately six to forty-eight [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] before being transformed into a rakghoul, one fully capable of spreading the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]-made disease on to further victims.

In the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before, during, and after the [[Mandalorian Wars]], the Rakghoul Plague spread nearly unchecked through the [[Undercity (Taris)|Undercity]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Taris/Legends|Taris]], and well over a million [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Neo-Crusaders]] fell victim to the plague's effects on the [[Water/Legends|ice]]-covered world of [[Jebble]]. Though the rakghouls were widely thought to have become extinct at a [[Time/Legends|time]] prior to the [[Declaration of a New Order|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Rakghoul Plague&mdash;and by extension, the rakghouls themselves&mdash;would continue to exist in the galaxy by the powers of the Muur Talisman until [[137 ABY]], when the dangerous [[Sith artifact/Legends|Sith artifact]] was finally [[Shatterpoint/Legends|destroyed]] by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Cade Skywalker]] on the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Imperial]] world of [[Had Abbadon]].

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|<nowiki />''Rakghouls''. In my time, they were a plague on Taris. I created the ones outside by willing it so. The talisman gives me that ability except in some nonhuman species&hellip;and individuals strong in the Force. The rakghouls began as creations of Karness Muur's Sith magic, but scratches or bites spread the plague&mdash;even to Force users like you.|[[Celeste Morne]] explains the rakghoul plague to [[Cade Skywalker]]|<ref name="LegacyVector" />}}
[[File:PlagueAtWork.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The rakghoul plague transforms a group of Imperials.]]
The primary means for the spread of the [[Sithspawn/Legends|Sith-spawned]] [[rakghoul]]s was through the [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]] of the [[Muur Talisman]], a [[Sith talisman/Legends|Sith amulet]] [[Sith alchemy/Legends|forged]] by the ancient [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]], [[Karness Muur]]. In the [[Limb/Legends|hands]] of Muur, or in the possession of another [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-user]] following Muur's [[Death/Legends|death]], the talisman's power transformed any [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] being without a connection to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] into a rakghoul.<ref name="LegacyVector" /> Even protective suits designed to shield a wearer from harmful germs or chemicals could not hold off the effects of the Sith magic.<ref name="DarkTimesVector">''[[Star Wars: Dark Times: Vector]]''</ref> But the rakghoul plague in its most infamous form existed as a [[virus]]-like disease, which Muur [[Sith alchemist/Legends|engineered]] as a means of circumventing the talisman's weakness: Force-sensitives and a number of [[Alien/Legends|non]]-[[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Species/Legends|species]] were immune to the effects of the talisman. This disease, as its name implied, was a plague that could be spread from an existing rakghoul by means of a [[Tooth/Legends|bite]] or scratch from its [[Claw/Legends|claw]], infecting the victim from even the smallest wound.<ref name="LegacyVector" /> Following contact with a rakghoul, the progression of the infection was a rapid and painful experience.<ref name="Wizards: Rakghoul" /> Incubation periods for the disease differed between species,<ref name="KotORVector" /> but a period of six to forty-eight [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] was typical. A victim's body would become twisted, and the pigmentation of the skin became paled to a [[white]]ned, corpse-like state,<ref name="Wizards: Rakghoul" /> and [[Blood/Legends|bleeding]] from the [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], mouth, and skin were not uncommon.<ref name="LegacyVector" /> Not long after this, the victim underwent a bodywide [[Mutant|mutation]],<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> their body growing and transforming into a rakghoul similar to the creature that infected them, and capable of spreading the rakghoul plague to another. This included the victim's five toes becoming feet with three big claws, spikes growing over their body, teeth becoming much larger, sharper, and deadlier, and hands becoming huge clawed tearing machines.<ref name="KotORVector" /> The transformation was usually very painful for any victim. In some cases a victim had been so badly injured by a rakghoul that they wanted the transformation to happen sooner so the pain would end.

Aside from its physical effects, the Rakghoul Plague had significant mental and psychological effects on its victims. Once transformed into a rakghoul, the original being's intelligence was seemingly lost, and most thought so little of the mental capacity of the common rakghoul as to denote them "mindless." In truth, however, the plague destroyed only the personality of the infected, leaving behind the being's knowledge and skills they had accumulated in their former lives. Left on their own, rakghouls behaved as beasts, serving their base instincts and existing as [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] to their own hunger. But if a being skilled in the [[Force power/Legends|powers of the Force]] were to wield the Muur Talisman, the rakghouls could draw upon those latent skills and abilities to be used in service to the talisman's possessor, even utilizing weapons and operating equipment. Unfortunately for the transformed beings, though, their original personalities could not be restored once they became rakghouls, and these seemingly more intelligent creatures operated only on an imprint left behind of their former lives.<ref name="KotORVector" />

===Variants===
{{Quote|What's the difference between a Hirano strain of the rakghoul virus and the Bozan variant?''"<br />"''Mutation of Clawdite-derived gene sequence.|Xenobiologists [[Ianna Cel]] and [[Eckard Lokin]] on their favorite topic|<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
There were two known variants of the Rakghoul Plague virus: the Bozan strain and the Hirano strain. They differed because of the mutation of a [[Clawdite/Legends|Clawdite]]-derived [[Gene/Legends|gene]] sequence, although it was not expanded on which was modified from which.

[[File:DarkForceHeal.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Cade Skywalker cures himself and Azlyn Rae of the Rakghoul Plague]]
The Rakghoul Plague was often thought to be without a cure, and that the most merciful option was to kill the unfortunate afflicted before the plague could be spread further,<ref name="KotORVector" /><ref name="LegacyVector" /> but there were two known methods that did indeed exist with the capability to halt the rakghoul transformation in a victim infected with the plague. A [[Rakghoul serum|serum]] had been found during the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Jedi Civil War]], by [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Darth Malak|Malak's]] [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]], and their [[Sith trooper (Sith Empire)|Sith troopers]] often carried vials of the curative serum on their person during trips into the [[Undercity (Taris)|Undercity]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Taris/Legends|Taris]], where the number of rakghouls was highest. The serum would be administered in the period of time prior to the victim's transformation, halting the progression of the infection and preventing the rakghoul mutation.<ref name="KotOR" /> Another means was discovered by a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] by the name of [[Cade Skywalker]] thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, [[137 ABY|during]] the [[Second Imperial Civil War]]. After [[Gender/Legends|he]] and his companion, [[Azlyn Rae]], had been infected with the Rakghoul Plague, Skywalker used his [[Dark transfer|radical healing ability]] to purge them of the plague, [[Force healing/Legends|curing]] and saving them both.<ref name="LegacyVector" />

==History==
===Introduction to the galaxy===
{{Quote|We ''saw'' rakghouls. The plague that creates them only exists in the Undercity of Taris.|[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Feln]]|<ref name="KotORVector" />}}
[[File:MorneKillsSowrs-KOTOR25.jpg|thumb|left|275px|Jedi Knight Celeste Morne cuts down the plague-infected [[Constable/Legends|constable]] of Taris]]
The Rakghoul Plague was originally created by the Sith Lord Karness Muur. Muur was one of the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Exiles]] who were [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|banished]] to the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]-controlled [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], following their defeat at the [[Battle of Corbos]] which ended the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]]. Like many of his contemporaries, Muur used the power of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] to manipulate life.<ref name="LegacyVector" /> Muur's prized achievement was the flesh-eating rakghouls<ref name="TCSWE" /> and he believed that the rakghouls would be the [[Army/Legends|army]] he would use to conquer [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], using the Rakghoul Plague to turn his enemies into his slaves.<ref name="KotORVector" /> Using his Sith magic, Muur could transform any nearby sentient into a mindless rakghoul, but he found there were exceptions, however, as both Force-sensitive beings and beings from a number of non-Human species proved immune to the talisman's effects. To combat this flaw, Muur engineered a new form of the Rakghoul Plague, a virus-like disease that could be spread from a rakghoul's bite or a scratch from its claws. The infected victim, no matter the species or Force-sensitivity, would then slowly mutate into a rakghoul within a timeframe spanning mere hours.<ref name="KotORVector" /><ref name="LegacyVector" /> Muur's ambitions for galactic conquest would be dashed after he was killed by jealous rivals, but Muur's [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] lived on through the Sith amulet he had forged in life, into which the Sith Lord had poured his mind, will, and the power to transform nearby beings into rakghouls. Possession of Muur's talisman was fleeting following his death,<ref name="LegacyVector" /> and eventually the talisman fell into the hands of a being who brought it to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] world of Taris where a cave in deep within the decrepit Undercity left the talisman's owner dead and the Sith amulet forgotten in the bowels of the planet.<ref name="KotORVector" /> There, the Rakghoul Plague ran rampant, and countless beings were infected. However, the government of Taris made little effort to fight the spread of the plague as it was contained in the lower levels of the [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|ecumenopolis]], a region occupied in large part by Taris' criminal underclass.<ref name="TCSWE" />

[[File:RakghoulCrusaders.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders transform into rakghouls after being infected with the Rakghoul Plague on Jebble.]]
It was not until the [[Mandalorian Wars]] that the talisman would be rediscovered, by a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Neo-Crusader]] search team led by the Mandalorian [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Pulsipher]]. Pulsipher took the talisman from Taris to the Mandalorian-held world, [[Jebble]], infecting a cadre of his [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] with the Rakghoul Plague aboard [[Mar'eyce|his ship]] while en route. There, the infected Mandalorians transformed into rakghouls and attacked their former comrades, spreading the plague further in a cascading chain that led to the transformation of almost every Mandalorian and Neo-Crusader recruit on Jebble. Pulsipher lost possession of the talisman to the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Celeste Morne]], who chose to entomb herself and the dangerous Sith artifact inside the Sith Lord [[Remulus Dreypa]]'s [[Dreypa's Oubliette|oubliette]]&mdash;on Jebble and among other Force-related items Pulsipher had been collecting&mdash;in order to prevent the further spread of the plague. Mandalorian [[Commander/Legends|commander]] [[Cassus Fett]], upon being warned of the rakghoul plague outbreak on the planet's surface by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Zayne Carrick]], chose to [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbitally bombard]] Jebble with [[Nuclear weapon/Legends|nuclear]] [[Missile/Legends|missiles]] in order to destroy the infection. The rakghouls were all destroyed in the attack, and the [[Oubliette (stasis casket)|oubliette]] containing Morne sunk beneath the [[Water/Legends|seas]] formed as Jebble's glaciers melted from the immense heat.<ref name="KotORVector" />

Though the Muur Talisman was gone, Taris continued to be afflicted by the Rakghoul Plague in the years leading up to the [[Jedi Civil War]]. The Undercity remained heavily infested and more were infected with the Rakghoul Plague regularly, after being scratched or bitten.<ref name="KotOR" /> By that point, it was estimated that over sixty million beings on the planet had been infected by the rakghoul plague.<ref name="Wizards: Rakghoul" /> The [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]] formed by the Jedi Knights-turned-Sith Lords [[Darth/Legends|Darths]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Darth Malak|Malak]] came to occupy Taris during the new war between their new Sith and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. With them came a curative serum for the Rakghoul Plague, capable of healing those infected by the Rakghoul Plague who had yet to complete the transformation, but the Sith restricted access to the serum to those Sith [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] that were sent into the Undercity.<ref name="KotOR" />
{{GameLS|Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic}}
An [[Amnesia/Legends|amnesiac]] Revan&mdash;his memory of his time as a Sith Lord after falling to the dark side removed by the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]]&mdash;later found a vial of the curative serum on the body of a dead Sith trooper while on Taris, and used it to heal several [[Outcasts (Taris)|Undercity residents]] infected with the Rakghoul Plague before finally giving it to the [[Upper City]] [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]] [[Zelka Forn]]. Forn used this sample to synthesize a mass-produced serum that could be sold at a low price to all Tarisians.<ref name="KotOR" />
{{Endgame}}
Shortly after, Taris was subjected to a [[Destruction of Taris|devastating orbital bombardment]] by Darth Malak's [[Sith armada (Lost Tribe of the Sith)|Sith armada]], killing an untold number of beings on the planet, including a significant number of rakghouls.<ref name="KotOR" />

===The Cold War===
{{Expandsect}}
However, many rakghouls survived the bombardment, and terrorized the Outcasts and other survivors. The Outcasts, who had rediscovered their [[Promised Land]]&mdash;which was actually the original Taris colony site&mdash;survived through use of the rakghoul serum that Revan had given them, but their later generations ran out of the serum and were eventually killed.<ref name="Chasing">{{TORcite|type=general|Chasing History|Taris (Republic)}}</ref>

[[File:Rakghoul_Plague_Infected_Reek.png|thumb|left|250px|A [[Reek/Legends|Reek]] infected with the Rakghoul Plague]]
Almost three hundred years after the bombardment, the Republic began a [[Taris Resettlement Initiative|resettlement project]] on the planet. Many believed that restoring the planet would serve as a symbol that the Republic would recover from the [[Great Galactic War]] and triumph over the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], and the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] established a presence there to protect the settlers. The rakghouls had thrived and once again terrorized the inhabitants of the planet, roaming the overgrown ruins of the city.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> Around [[3643 BBY]], a group of rakghouls was discovered in the eastern [[Tularan Marsh]] that had been exposed to a mixture of chemicals and radiation, mutating and strengthening them.<ref name="Mutations">{{TORcite|type=heroic|Mutations|Taris (Republic)}}</ref>

Around that time, Professor [[Sadus Vraal]] and [[Mola Haxtor]] discovered that a subspecies of rakghoul had developed nearby&mdash;the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[nekghoul]]s. With the help of a Republic-allied individual, they investigated the factory that the nekghouls were inhabiting, but the individual discovered that the [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] of [[Bay-Yon Siu]], a Jedi of the [[Sanej Temple]], was teaching the nekghouls. The Jedi Knight [[Danah Jor]] had attempted to destroy the nekghouls, but had been captured, and Siu convinced the individual to allow the nekghouls to live while he taught them the ways of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]].<ref name="Darkness">{{TORcite|type=general|Where Darkness Abides|Taris (Republic)}}</ref>

The [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] scientist Doctor [[Sannus Lorrick]] weaponized and [[Tion Hegemony rakghoul outbreak|released]] a strain of the plague on the planet [[Kaon]] to get revenge on the [[Tion Hegemony/Legends|Tion Hegemony]] for disgracing him. He fled to [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]], where he set up an [[Lost Island|island]] base and continued his experiments.

Lorrick also gave an infected [[risp]] to the smuggler [[Zama Brak]], who boarded the [[Passenger liner/Legends|passenger liner]] ''[[Stardream]]'' departing Ord Mantell. The risp spread the plague among almost all of the crew and the 492 passengers aboard in the matter of fifteen days, causing the infected [[Captain/Legends|captain]] [[Magnus (Galactic War)|Magnus]] to crash the ship into the [[Dune Sea/Legends|Dune Sea]] on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. As the ship broke up on its descent, it spread wreckage and escape pods filled with infected passengers across the Dune Sea and the neighboring [[Jundland Wastes/Legends|Jundland Wastes]], forcing both the Republic and the Empire to declare the planet a quarantine zone. Imperial and Republic containment troops deployed immediately to the planet, stopping all infected from leaving the planet. The plague also infected many of the native [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] and wildlife, including [[Bantha/Legends|banthas]], [[Reek/Legends|reeks]], and [[wraid]]s. The outbreak would eventually turn into a massive [[Rakghoul pandemic|pandemic]].<ref name="Pandemic">{{TORcite|World Event: "Rakghoul Pandemic"}}</ref>

===Outbreak===
====Awakening====
[[File:GonnaNeedAFacelift.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Fane Peturri falls victim to the Rakghoul Plague]]
{{Quote|It is the ''rakghoul plague''. Did you really believe a suit designed to protect you from germs and viruses would shield you from the effects of Sith magic?|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]|<ref name="DarkTimesVector" />}}
Over time, the rakghouls were isolated on Taris and&mdash;likely due in part to the serum Revan recovered&mdash;driven to extinction.<ref name="DarkTimesVector" /> However, while the Muur Talisman remained, the threat of the rakghouls did as well. Approximately fourteen hundred years before the galaxy-spanning [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], ice miners discovered the oubliette of Dreypa beneath the surface of Jebble. A mystery to it finders, the oubliette became known as the "Jebble Box," and the inability to open it or [[Scanner|scan]] what was inside bred numerous rumors as to its origins. Collectors bought and sold the box they believed to be an ancient Jedi treasure, and wars were even fought over the mysterious object. In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the crew of the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] ''[[Uhumele]]'' brought the box to a [[Unidentified desert moon|desolate moon]] with the intent to sell it to the scholar and antiquities collector [[Fane Peturri]]; Peturri was in league with [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] and his [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], and the [[Color/Legends|black]]-[[Armor/Legends|armored]] Sith Lord released Celeste Morne from stasis. Upon finding her rescuer to be a Sith, Morne [[First duel on unidentified desert moon|attacked]] Vader and [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|engaged]] him in a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|battle]] of [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]]. When Vader proved too powerful, Morne was forced to use the Muur Talisman to unleash the rakghoul plague and save herself, transforming Vader's [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] into rakghouls that subsequently attacked their former commander. Vader fled, but the activation of the talisman's magic had an unintended side effect: the talisman transformed the only [[Crys Taanzer|human member]] of the ''Uhumele''{{'s}} crew into a rakghoul as well, and the [[Schurk-Heren|ship's captain]] was forced to kill her. Vader fled, as did the ''Uhumele'' crew, leaving Morne alone on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] with only the rakghouls she had spawned and the spirit of Karness Muur for company.<ref name="DarkTimesVector" />

====Spreading infection====
{{Quote|Now&hellip;why do you think these two aren't affected by the rakghoul plague?|[[Karness Muur]], discovering [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa's]] Force-sensitivity|<ref name="RebellionVector">''[[Star Wars: Rebellion: Vector]]''</ref>}}
[[File:StormtroopersRakghouls-Rebellion-15.png|thumb|left|250px|An Imperial stormtrooper scouting party is transformed into rakghouls]]
Close to twenty years passed, but Vader did not forget the events that transpired on that barren moon. Nine [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Vader ordered a [[Scout/Legends|scouting]] party to the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] moon to ascertain the fate of Morne. When the [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] of stormtroopers neared the moon's surface, Morne [[Telekinesis/Legends|used the Force]] to drag the shuttle down before transforming everyone aboard with the talisman-borne rakghoul plague.<ref name="RebellionVector" /> Now sure that Morne did indeed still live, Vader tasked his [[Spy/Legends|spy]], [[Wyl Tarson]], with instructions to leak word of a secret Imperial weapon located on the moon, and ensure that it was noticed by members of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], a group of rebels that had been [[Declaration of Rebellion/Legends|formed]] in the years since Vader had first confronted Morne as a force to oppose the oppressive Empire and restore the Republic that it had once been. A small team of "Rebel Alliance" members traveled to the moon, unable to resist the lure of the potential victory over their Imperial enemies. Almost immediately upon setting down, however, the strike team was beset by Morne's rakghoul horde, and a number of them were infected by the Rakghoul Plague during the resulting skirmish. One group of rebels escaped the attack aboard [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo's]] personal ship, the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], while rebel leader [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and friend [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] were momentarily left behind with the former [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]], [[Able]].<ref name="RebellionVector" />

[[File:UnderstatementOfTheYear.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Rakghoul Plague claims a member of the Rebel Alliance]]
Morne, having suffered through nearly twenty years with none but the corrupting presence of Karness Muur's spirit as a companion, had become convinced that the Jedi had abandoned her and attacked the Force-sensitive Skywalker. When Organa attempted to assist him and Morne turned her blade on her instead, Able rushed to the Princess' defense only to fall victim to the Rakghoul Plague and be transformed into a rakghoul. When Muur's spirit realized the untapped Force potential within both Skywalker and Organa, he detached his talisman's hold on Morne and attacked Skywalker. Coming to her senses, Morne batted the Sith amulet away and retook the burden onto herself. Her control over Muur regained, Morne turned away from the two rebels and boarded the shuttle they had arrived on the moon with, and departed with her [[Legion/Legends|legion]] of rakghouls, leaving Skywalker and Organa to flee aboard the returned ''Millennium Falcon''. As she passed out of the moon's [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]], Morne flew by a waiting [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class]] [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]], turning the crew into rakghouls with the talisman's plague before vanishing into [[Realspace/Legends|space]] as the [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] crashed into the surface of the moon and was destroyed.<ref name="RebellionVector" />

===A partial remedy===
{{Quote|This is an ancient Sith alchemy, my lord. There is a holocron that speaks of creatures who caused a plague on ancient ''Taris''&hellip;the festering wounds he suffered resembled the infectious bite of these '<nowiki></nowiki>''rakghoul'.|[[Darth Maladi]]|<ref name="LegacyVector" />}}
[[File:Welcometotheclub.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A rakghoul's scratch infects Azlyn Rae with the plague aboard the Star Destroyer ''Iron Sun''.]]
Over a hundred years passed as Morne traveled the galaxy, before being taken aboard the [[Pellaeon-class Star Destroyer|''Pellaeon''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Iron Sun]]'' in [[127 ABY]]. Believing the [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] to be in the employ of the Empire she had awoken to under Vader and Palpatine, Morne unleashed the rakghoul plague upon the Star [[Destroyer/Legends|Destroyer]], transforming the ''Iron Sun''{{'s}} crew into a new rakghoul army. Another ten years passed before the commandeered ''Iron Sun'' took on new captives: the crew of the [[Mynock (Helot-class)|''Mynock'']], led by Cade Skywalker and on a mission to [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] the current [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], [[Darth Krayt]]. The crew was shortly attacked by rakghouls, and during their efforts to repel the beastly aggressors, Skywalker was bitten and his [[Imperial Knight]] companion, Azlyn Rae, scratched, both becoming infected with the Rakghoul Plague. Celeste Morne was able to halt the rakghouls' attack after reasserting control, but when she discovered the two had been infected, the Jedi took it upon herself to isolate Skywalker and Rae from their companions, imprisoning them within a detention cell while she promised each a swift death after the transformation occurred. To her surprise, however, Skywalker was able to use his tremendous Force-healing ability to cure himself and Rae of the plague, impressing Morne and earning the ''Mynock'' crew a new ally against Krayt.<ref name="LegacyVector" />

[[File:RakghoulReave.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Reave succumbs to his rakghoul-inflicted wounds and transforms into a rakghoul.]]
Skywalker's team launched an [[Mission to Had Abbadon|attack]] on the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Imperial]] base located on the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] planet of [[Had Abbadon]], shortly after. There, Morne transformed a number of the base's stormtroopers into rakghouls, who then aided the group in battle against the [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] Sith Lord, [[Darth Reave]]. Reave was wounded by the rakghouls, and fled back to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] where he delivered a report to Darth Krayt at the [[Temple of the Sith]]. During the meeting, Reave succumbed to the effects of the rakghoul plague and transformed into a rakghoul, attacking his former Sith allies before being [[Sai cha/Legends|struck down]] by [[Darth Stryfe]]. Taking the bait laid before them, Krayt and a cadre of his loyal Sith traveled to Had Abbadon where they were [[Battle on Had Abbadon|ambushed]] by Skywalker and his group; Morne unleashed her rakghoul horde on Darth Krayt, but the combined force of Krayt's [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] and Darth Stryfe's protective lightsaber defense cut the rakghouls down in droves. Still, the Sith fell to Skywalker's team and Krayt himself was dealt a [[Shiak|mortal wound]] by Azlyn Rae that left everyone involved believing Krayt dead. In the battle's aftermath, Morne asked that Skywalker end her life, knowing she was losing her battle for control with the spirit of Karness Muur. Skywalker solemnly granted her wish and took her life with his lightsaber, only for the Muur Talisman to target Skywalker as its new host. However, Skywalker had no interest in the power Muur offered, and instead [[Shatterpoint/Legends|used the Force]] to destroy the talisman once and for all, putting an end to its ability to spread the rakghoul plague. Though the Muur Talisman was gone, any rakghouls that continued to live after the events on Had Abbadon, still carried the potential to spread the Rakghoul Plague to other victims.<ref name="LegacyVector" />
